newsitem.title: THAILAND: GOLF-PETTERS IS A KNOCKOUT IN BANGKOK CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PETTERS IS A KNOCKOUT IN BANGKOK CLASSIC.

text.p: Dubai-based Englishman Lee Petters made light of being whacked in the face by his playing partner's driver, going on to shoot a six-under-par 66 in the first round of the Bangkok Classic on Thursday.
Petters, a professional at the Dubai Creek Golf and Yacht Club, led by a stroke from Thailand's Prayad Marksaeng and American Clay Devers.
Tiger Woods, the tournament's drawcard, finished four shots off the pace.

Petters' finest moment in his four-year professional career came close to ending in disaster when Pakistan's Shakeel Hussain accidentally hit him in the face with his driver as they walked off the 14th tee.
"I was knocked straight to the floor," said Petters. "There was blood everywhere. I was on the ground for about five or 10 minutes.
"When the doctor came he said I had to go off to get the wound stitched but being four under for my round at the time there was no way I was going to leave."
After the blood was mopped up, Petters proceeded to birdie the next hole -- a 602-yard par five. He also birdied the par five 17th.
Woods, who failed to finish his pro-am round on Wednesday because of heat exhaustion, completed his first round in Thailand -- his mother's homeland -- in joint 15th place.

"I felt a little bit better today," Woods told a packed news conference. "But as far as playing goes I'll have to shape up. Today was kind of scratch. I made a lot of mental mistakes and some physical ones as well...I have to tighten up the screws a bit."
The American, who has been given a hero's welcome by Thais eager to welcome him as their "native son", appeared somewhat nonplussed over the huge media interest in him.
He is reportedly receiving $500,000 to compete in the tournament.
